source_refs.note: Book p. 183: 6.3 Parabola, definition (locus; focus; directrix) before 6.3.1.

blocks.text: A Parabola is the locus of a point which moves in a plane such that its distance from a fixed point, called the focus, is equal to its distance from a given fixed straight line, called the directrix.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
What does "locus" mean? A locus is the path traced by a point that obeys a rule. Here the rule is: (distance from the focus) = (distance from the directrix). Every point that obeys this rule lies on the parabola, and every point of the parabola obeys it.
In symbols: if \(F\) is the focus and \(PM\) is the perpendicular from a point \(P\) to the directrix, then \(P\) is on the parabola exactly when
\[|PF| = |PM|\]
The distance to a line is always the perpendicular (shortest) distance.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Where do we meet parabolas? The path of a ball thrown at an angle, the jet of water from a fountain, the cable of a suspension bridge and the cross-section of a satellite dish or a car headlight are (very nearly) parabolas. In Section 6.6 the book uses the parabola's reflecting property for such problems.

blocks.title: Teaching note
Key points
blocks.text:
1. Parabola: set of points equally distant from a fixed point (focus) and a fixed line (directrix).
2. The test for any point \(P\): \(|PF| = |PM|\), where \(PM\) is the perpendicular distance to the directrix.
3. The focus never lies on the directrix.
4. Distance from a point \((x_{1}, y_{1})\) to the line \(Ax + By + C = 0\) is \(\frac{|Ax_{1} + By_{1} + C|}{\sqrt{A^{2} + B^{2}}}\); we use it in every parabola question built from the definition.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text:
1. Measuring the distance to the directrix along a slanted line. It must be the perpendicular distance.
2. Thinking the focus is a point on the curve. The focus is inside the curve's opening; the vertex is the point of the curve nearest to it.
3. Mixing the definition of a circle (fixed distance from one point) with that of a parabola (equal distances from a point and a line).
